official.description: Each year Lund University awards a selective, merit-based scholarship programme to new high-achieving international students from outside the EU/EEA who are applying for degree programmes. Lund states that it awards approximately SEK 26 million in scholarship grants each year, and that the scholarship is highly selective and based entirely on merit.

verification.notes: Live-fetched the Lund University Global Scholarship page (last updated 26 Aug 2026). The only monetary figure the university publishes is the aggregate annual budget of approximately SEK 26 million (EUR 2.3 million / USD 2.7 million) across all grants, which is a programme total, not a per-student award; no individual amount or percentage is published, so funding_amount stays null. Coverage wording ('tuition fees only - living costs are not included'), the 16 February 2026 closing date and the 600-word motivation letter requirement are all taken verbatim from that page.

applicant_utility.summary: Read the fine print on what you are actually competing for: Lund says grants may cover part or all of the tuition and that the percentage awarded depends on the programme or faculty budget rather than your academic record, so two equally strong candidates can receive very different awards. The award letter arrives shortly after the admission result and names the amount, and the scholarship is deducted from your tuition invoice automatically. Because the award never touches living costs, you must satisfy the Swedish Migration Agency's funding requirement on your own even if you win. The single highest-leverage administrative decision is ranking your Lund programme first at universityadmissions.se, since the first-choice status is both an eligibility rule and an explicit selection priority.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland with a consistently strong transcript who have a genuine first-choice Lund programme and independent funding for living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Rank the Lund programme as your first choice at universityadmissions.se before you even think about the scholarship
Pay the national application fee and confirm the application shows as complete before the scholarship round opens
Write a 600-word Scholarship Motivation Letter that is separate from the programme statement of purpose and explains your academic achievements plus your reasons for choosing Lund
Watch the scholarship page from early February, because the portal link only appears once the round opens
Plan around a two-track result timeline: admission notification first, scholarship outcome shortly afterwards
common_rejection_risks: Lund not being ranked first at universityadmissions.se, which alone disqualifies the application
Submitting the scholarship application before the national application is complete and the fee is paid
Pasting the programme statement of purpose into the scholarship portal instead of a distinct motivation letter
Exceeding the 600-word limit on the Scholarship Motivation Letter
Assuming financial need helps - the university states plainly that financial need is not considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Sweden (accommodation, food, insurance, transport), travel, and the remaining tuition instalment if only a partial reduction is granted.
